findings.title: align=False crashes with 'unknown model: False' despite docstring 'If False or None, no alignment is applied'
findings.description: analyze()'s align docstring explicitly permits False ('If False or None, no alignment is applied (default: None)'), but passing align=False raises ValueError on BOTH the legacy path and the pipeline path (return_model=True). tools/align.py only special-cases None (and True, with a curated removal message); False falls through to the dispatcher as a model name. Related path inconsistency: align=True gets the curated 'align=True was removed in hypertools 1.0...' message on the legacy path but the cryptic 'unknown model: True' on the pipeline path (build_pipeline only special-cases normalize=False, not align=False/True).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
data = [rng.standard_normal((30, 6)) for _ in range(2)]
hyp.analyze(data, normalize='within', align=False)
findings.expected: No alignment applied; normalized data returned (per analyze() docstring for align).
findings.actual: ValueError: unknown model: False  (same with return_model=True; align=True on the pipeline path gives 'ValueError: unknown model: True' instead of the curated removal message)

findings.title: reduce='TSNE' (or 'MDS') + cluster= crashes with AttributeError after fitting everything
findings.description: When cluster= is given, analyze() re-derives the pre-cluster transformed data by re-applying each fitted non-cluster step via .transform (analyze.py lines 178-183). For embedding models with no .transform (TSNE, MDS, SpectralEmbedding -- all listed as supported reduce models in analyze's docstring), Reducer.transform calls model.transform and crashes. Happens with AND without return_model=True, after all fitting work is done. The same fitted pipelines also cannot be reused via pipeline=/Pipeline.transform for the same reason.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
small = [rng.standard_normal((25, 5)) for _ in range(2)]
hyp.analyze(small, reduce={'model': 'TSNE', 'kwargs': {'perplexity': 5}}, ndims=2,
            cluster={'model': 'KMeans', 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 2, 'n_init': 10}}, random_state=0)
findings.expected: TSNE-embedded data returned (labels recoverable from the fitted cluster step), or a clear up-front error that TSNE cannot be combined with cluster=.

findings.title: pipeline= reuse of a cluster-bearing model returns cluster LABELS, not transformed data (contract flips between fit and reuse)
findings.description: analyze()'s cluster= docs promise 'analyze still returns the TRANSFORMED DATA (not cluster labels) when cluster= is given', and the fit path implements that via the re-derivation loop. But the pipeline= branch just calls pipeline.transform(data), whose last step IS the cluster step -- so the natural fit-then-apply workflow (fit with return_model=True on session 1, pipeline= on session 2) silently returns a 1-D label sequence on reuse where the fit call returned (n, ndims) data. hyp.plot(..., pipeline=...) routes through the same branch (plot/plot.py:1671).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(0)
train, test = rng.standard_normal((60, 10)), rng.standard_normal((60, 10))
out_tr, model = hyp.analyze(train, normalize='across', reduce='PCA', ndims=2,
                            cluster={'model': 'KMeans', 'kwargs': {'n_clusters': 3, 'n_init': 10, 'random_state': 0}},
                            return_model=True)
out_te = hyp.analyze(test, pipeline=model)
print(np.asarray(out_tr).shape, np.asarray(out_te).shape)
findings.expected: Both calls return transformed data of shape (60, 2), per the documented cluster= return contract; labels retrievable via model.named_steps['cluster'].
findings.actual:
fit-path return: ndarray (60, 2)
reuse-path return: list (60,) first5: [1 0 0 2 0]  -- cluster labels, not data

findings.title: pipeline= docstring claims ndims=/impute= 'are still honored' -- both are silently ignored (impute falls back to PPCA)
findings.description: The pipeline= parameter docs state '`ndims=`/`internal=`/`impute=` are still honored'. In the pipeline= branch only internal= is implemented: data is passed straight to pipeline.transform, so impute='Kalman' on NaN data produces output bit-identical to the PPCA default (verified allclose), and ndims=4 with a model fit at ndims=2 still returns 2 columns. Either thread impute= through format_data on this path (as the pipeline-BUILD path does at analyze.py lines 153-164) or fix the docstring.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
data = [rng.standard_normal((30, 6)) for _ in range(2)]
nan_data = [x.copy() for x in data]; nan_data[0][3, 2] = np.nan; nan_data[1][10, 5] = np.nan
_, m = hyp.analyze(data, normalize='across', reduce='PCA', ndims=2, return_model=True)
ra = hyp.analyze(nan_data, pipeline=m, impute='Kalman')
rb = hyp.analyze(nan_data, pipeline=m)
print(all(np.allclose(a, b) for a, b in zip(ra, rb)))  # True -> impute ignored
print([np.asarray(o).shape[1] for o in hyp.analyze(data, pipeline=m, ndims=4)])  # [2, 2] -> ndims ignored
findings.expected: impute='Kalman' changes the imputation used (as it does on the other two paths); ndims honored or documented as encoded in the pipeline.
findings.actual:
impute= ignored on pipeline= path (identical): True
pipeline= with ndims=4 (model fit with ndims=2) -> cols: [2, 2]

findings.title: Misspelled HyperAlign kwargs are silently accepted (align={'model':'HyperAlign','kwargs':{'n_itr':0}} runs as n_iter=10)
findings.description: HyperAlign accepts **kwargs, so a typo'd parameter in the align dict spec is swallowed without error or warning. Proven behaviorally: n_itr=0 (typo) produces output allclose-identical to the n_iter=10 default and different from n_iter=0. A scientist who mistypes a parameter believes it took effect. reduce/cluster dict specs correctly raise TypeError naming the bad kwarg (PCA/KMeans do constructor validation); the align stage is the silent one. Root cause is in hypertools/align (Aligner **kwargs), surfaced through analyze's documented dict-spec grammar.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(3)
data = [rng.standard_normal((30, 6)) for _ in range(2)]
a_typo = hyp.analyze(data, align={'model': 'HyperAlign', 'kwargs': {'n_itr': 0}})
a_default = hyp.analyze(data, align='hyper')
a_zero = hyp.analyze(data, align={'model': 'HyperAlign', 'kwargs': {'n_iter': 0}})
print(all(np.allclose(a, b) for a, b in zip(a_typo, a_default)))  # True
print(all(np.allclose(a, b) for a, b in zip(a_typo, a_zero)))     # False
findings.expected: TypeError/ValueError naming the unknown parameter 'n_itr' (as the reduce and cluster stages do).
findings.actual:
typo n_itr==default(n_iter=10): True
typo n_itr==n_iter=0: False  -- no error, no warning

findings.title: reduce docstring claims '(default: IncrementalPCA)' but default is None -- analyze(data, ndims=3) silently does nothing
findings.description: analyze()'s reduce parameter docs say 'Decomposition/manifold learning model to use (default: \'IncrementalPCA\')' but the signature default is reduce=None, which SKIPS the stage entirely: analyze(data, ndims=3) (with or without normalize=, on both paths) returns full-dimensional data and silently ignores ndims. Behavior matches pre-1.0 master (byte-compat goal), but master's docstring made no default claim -- the false '(default: IncrementalPCA)' text was added in 1.0. Fix the docstring; consider also warning when ndims= is given while the reduce stage is skipped (silent no-op on an explicit user request).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
data = [rng.standard_normal((30, 6)) for _ in range(2)]
print([o.shape for o in hyp.analyze(data, ndims=3)])  # [(30, 6), (30, 6)] -- not reduced
findings.expected: Per docstring: reduction with IncrementalPCA to 3 dims -- or a docstring stating reduce=None skips reduction and ndims requires reduce=.
findings.actual: CASE | ndims=3 alone (reduce left None) | list len=2 shapes=[(30, 6), (30, 6)]  (same with normalize= and with return_model=True); no warning emitted

findings.title: analyze tutorial teaches the deprecated legacy dict spec and emits DeprecationWarning when run
findings.description: docs/tutorials/analyze.ipynb cell 21 uses reduce={'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'whiten': True}} -- the LEGACY dict form. Running the cell verbatim emits "DeprecationWarning: {'model': ..., 'params': {...}} is deprecated; use {'model': ..., 'args': [...], 'kwargs': {...}} instead". The 1.0 tutorial should teach the canonical kwargs form (which analyze's own docstring uses).
findings.repro:
import hypertools as hyp, warnings
weights = hyp.load('weights_avg')
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    reduce = {'model': 'PCA', 'params': {'whiten': True}}
    hyp.analyze(weights, normalize='within', reduce=reduce, ndims=3)
print([str(x.message) for x in w])
findings.expected: Tutorial code runs warning-free using the canonical dict spec.

findings.title: Invalid normalize value raises AssertionError naming nonexistent parameter 'scale_type'
findings.description: analyze(data, normalize='banana') (and normalize=True) surfaces tools/normalize.py's assert: 'AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.' The parameter is called normalize everywhere in the 1.0 API ('scale_type' does not exist), and AssertionError is the wrong exception type (vanishes under python -O; siblings raise ValueError).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.analyze([np.random.rand(10, 3)], normalize='banana')
findings.expected: ValueError: normalize must be 'across', 'within', 'row', False, None, or a fitted Normalizer; got 'banana'
findings.actual: AssertionError: scale_type must be across, within, row, none, or a fitted Normalizer.

findings.title: pipeline= + normalize=False raises the mutual-exclusion ValueError although False is documented as 'skip this stage'
findings.description: The conflict check tests `value is not None`, so normalize=False (documented as 'the input data will be returned with no z-scoring', and treated as stage-skip by build_pipeline itself) is reported as a conflicting stage kwarg. analyze(data, pipeline=m, normalize=False) should behave like normalize=None.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(1)
data = [rng.standard_normal((30, 6)) for _ in range(2)]
_, m = hyp.analyze(data, normalize='across', reduce='PCA', ndims=2, return_model=True)
hyp.analyze(data, pipeline=m, normalize=False)
findings.expected: Works like pipeline=m alone (False = stage disabled, consistent with build_pipeline's own normalize=False handling).
findings.actual: ValueError: pipeline= is mutually exclusive with the stage kwarg(s) normalize (a fitted Pipeline already encodes which stages run and their fitted parameters); pass pipeline= alone.

findings.title: pipeline= accepts any object; a non-Pipeline gives cryptic AttributeError
findings.description: No type/is-fitted check on pipeline= beyond duck-typing: analyze(data, pipeline='PCA') raises AttributeError: 'str' object has no attribute 'transform'. A short isinstance check would give a helpful message naming the parameter and expected type.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.analyze(np.random.rand(10, 3), pipeline='PCA')
findings.expected: TypeError/ValueError: pipeline= expects a fitted hypertools.Pipeline (got str).

findings.title: 3-D array input: silently returns axis-mangled data (constant values) or crashes deep in normalize (typical values)
findings.description: format_data does not reject 3-D arrays. analyze(np.zeros((4,5,6)), normalize='across') returns a silently TRANSPOSED (6,4,5) array; with non-constant values the same call crashes at tools/normalize.py:47 (_zscore_column 'if std == 0:') with 'ValueError: The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous'. fMRI users routinely hold 3-D arrays; this should be a clear 'expected 2-D data' error.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
print(hyp.analyze(np.zeros((4, 5, 6)), normalize='across').shape)  # (6, 4, 5) silently
hyp.analyze(np.arange(120.).reshape(4, 5, 6), normalize='across')  # crashes
findings.expected: ValueError naming the input problem (e.g. 'each dataset must be 2-D (samples x features); got shape (4, 5, 6)').
findings.actual: shape (6, 4, 5) returned silently for constant input; for non-constant input: ValueError: The truth value of an array with more than one element is ambiguous. Use a.any() or a.all() (from tools/normalize.py:47)

findings.title: Single-dataset return type varies by stage combo (bare array vs list-of-1 vs DataFrames); Returns docstring says 'list of numpy arrays'
findings.description: For a single 2-D array input: normalize-only and reduce-only return a bare ndarray; any combo including align returns a LIST of 1 array (tools/align.py always wraps); manip-only returns a list of pandas DATAFRAMES; the no-stage identity path returns the input object itself (DataFrame stays DataFrame). The Returns section flatly promises 'analyzed_data : list of numpy arrays'. Downstream code written against one combo breaks on another.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
arr = np.random.rand(30, 6)
print(type(hyp.analyze(arr, normalize='within')))            # ndarray
print(type(hyp.analyze(arr, align='hyper')))                 # list (len 1)
print([type(x).__name__ for x in hyp.analyze([arr, arr + 1], manip='ZScore')])  # DataFrames
findings.expected: One consistent convention (single-in -> single-out everywhere, or always list), matching an accurate Returns section.
findings.actual: normalize='within' -> ndarray (30, 6); align='hyper' -> list len=1; manip='ZScore' -> types=['DataFrame', 'DataFrame']

findings.title: reduce='banana' error omits supported names and cites a pre-1.0 docs URL (hypertools.tools.reduce)
findings.description: Unknown align/cluster/manip names produce 'unknown X model ...; supported names: ...' errors; unknown reduce names instead produce a vaguer message pointing at http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html -- a module path that no longer exists in 1.0 (reduce moved to hypertools/reduce/). The URL currently resolves only because readthedocs 'latest' still hosts the 0.8 docs; it will dangle after the 1.0 docs deploy.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.analyze([np.random.rand(10, 3)], reduce='banana', ndims=2)
findings.expected: ValueError listing supported reduce model names, styled like the align/cluster/manip errors, with a current docs link (if any).
findings.actual: ValueError: reduce must be one of the supported options or support n_components and fit_transform methods. See http://hypertools.readthedocs.io/en/latest/hypertools.tools.reduce.html#hypertools.tools.reduce for supported models

findings.title: random_state parameter is accepted and routed but entirely undocumented in analyze's docstring
findings.description: analyze(..., random_state=) is in the signature, is forwarded to the reduce stage (legacy path) and to build_pipeline (reduce+cluster stages), and verified working (TSNE reproducible across calls with random_state=42), but the docstring's Parameters section never mentions it.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp, inspect
print('random_state' in inspect.signature(hyp.analyze).parameters)  # True
print('random_state' in hyp.analyze.__doc__)  # False
findings.expected: random_state documented like hypertools.reduce.reduce's random_state section.
findings.actual: signature has random_state; docstring does not mention it (verified True/False above); reproducibility itself works (TSNE identical across two random_state=42 calls)

findings.title: ndims greater than n_features is a silent no-op (no warning), returning full-dimensional data
findings.description: analyze(data, reduce='PCA', ndims=10) on 6-feature data returns the 6-column data unchanged with zero warnings (warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) captured none). The user explicitly requested a 10-dim projection; a warning (as the dims/n_components mismatch case already emits) would prevent silent surprises.
findings.repro:
import warnings, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
data = [rng.standard_normal((30, 6)) for _ in range(2)]
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    warnings.simplefilter('always')
    out = hyp.analyze(data, reduce='PCA', ndims=10)
print([o.shape for o in out], [str(x.message) for x in w])
findings.expected: A UserWarning that ndims >= n_features so no reduction was performed.

findings.title: impute= is silently dropped when normalize= is not requested, even though PPCA imputation still runs
findings.description: The impute docs say it is 'applied at the format_data stage, when normalization triggers it', and the code gates impute-threading on `normalize not in (False, None)`. But with reduce-only calls, format_data STILL runs inside the reduce stage and STILL imputes NaNs -- just always with PPCA, ignoring the user's explicit impute= choice: analyze(nan_data, reduce='PCA', ndims=2, impute='Kalman') is allclose-identical to the same call without impute=. Either honor impute= wherever format_data imputes, or warn that it is being ignored.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
rng = np.random.default_rng(7)
nan_data = [rng.standard_normal((30, 6)) for _ in range(2)]
nan_data[0][3, 2] = np.nan
r1 = hyp.analyze(nan_data, reduce='PCA', ndims=2, impute='Kalman')
r2 = hyp.analyze(nan_data, reduce='PCA', ndims=2)
print(all(np.allclose(a, b) for a, b in zip(r1, r2)))  # True -> Kalman ignored, PPCA used
findings.expected: impute='Kalman' takes effect whenever imputation happens, or a warning that impute= requires normalize=.
findings.actual: impute= silently ignored without normalize= (identical): True  -- NaNs were imputed via PPCA regardless
